Finding the right 3D assets is one of the most time-consuming parts of game development. Fortunately, the game dev community is filled with incredibly generous creators and platforms offering high-quality, free assets. 

The best places to find free 3D game assets are categorized below by art style and use case.

---

### 1. Best for Low-Poly & Stylized Assets (Indie, Retro, & Game Jams)
If you are prototyping, participating in a game jam, or making a stylized/mobile game, these creators and platforms offer cohesive, easily integrated assets under **CC0 (Public Domain)** licenses (meaning they are free for personal and commercial use with no attribution required).

*   **Kenney (kenney.nl):** Known as the "King of Free Game Assets". Kenney offers over 40,000 completely free, modular assets (3D, 2D, audio, and UI). The 3D packs cover genres like sci-fi, fantasy, sports, platformers, and vehicles—all sharing a consistent, clean art style. 
*   **Quaternius (quaternius.com):** An incredibly prolific 3D artist who releases massive, highly polished, game-ready low-poly kits under CC0. Their library includes fully rigged and animated characters, modular dungeon and sci-fi kits, vehicles, and a "Universal Animation Library" with over 120+ retargetable humanoid animations.
*   **KayKit (kaylousberg.com):** Created by Kay Lousberg, this is another stellar library of cute, low-poly, CC0 game assets. You can download packs for dungeon crawlers, medieval settings, character animations, skeletons, and modular adventure characters.
*   **Poly Pizza (poly.pizza):** A dedicated search engine for low-poly 3D models. It hosts thousands of optimized models uploaded by various creators. It requires no login and is perfect for finding specific props, foods, or environment pieces quickly.

---

### 2. Best for Realistic & High-Fidelity Assets
If you are building a next-gen, photorealistic game, these platforms offer professional-grade textures and models.

*   **Poly Haven (polyhaven.com):** A 100% free, community-funded public asset library. Unlike other sites, everything here is CC0, meaning you don't even have to sign up to download. It is the gold standard for high-res photogrammetry 3D models, seamless PBR textures, and unclipped HDRIs for realistic lighting.
*   **Fab (fab.com):** Epic Games' unified marketplace (which consolidated Sketchfab, the Unreal Engine Marketplace, and Quixel Megascans). While Fab is a paid marketplace, it has a massive library of free, high-end 3D models, including highly optimized Quixel Megascans. Epic Games also gives away premium packs for free every two weeks. 
*   **3Dassets.one:** A incredibly useful aggregator search engine that lets you search across 15+ different free PBR texture and 3D model websites at once, saving you from having to search dozens of tabs.

---

### 3. Specialty Libraries (Rigging & Animation)
Rigging characters and animating them from scratch is incredibly difficult. These tools take care of it for free.

*   **Mixamo (mixamo.com):** Owned by Adobe, Mixamo is completely free. You can upload any humanoid 3D character (or use their default characters), and the platform will automatically rig it for you. You can then apply and download thousands of professional, motion-captured animations (walking, fighting, dancing, etc.) in `.FBX` format, ready for Unity, Unreal Engine, or Godot.

---

### 4. General Game Dev Marketplaces
These are massive platforms with active communities. You will need to use their search filters to isolate the free 3D models.

*   **itch.io (Game Assets Section):** While famous for hosting indie games, itch.io is one of the best places to find free game development kits. Go to the game assets section, click "3D", and filter by "Free". Many creators release base models, retro PSX-style assets, and modular kits here.
*   **Unity Asset Store:** If you use the Unity Engine, the Unity Asset Store has a massive "Free Assets" section. You can find complete environment packages, character models, and gameplay systems. *(Note: Many of these can be exported to other engines like Godot, but check the license first).*
*   **CGTrader & TurboSquid:** These are primarily commercial marketplaces for professional 3D artists, but both feature robust "Free" filters. They are great sources for highly detailed, specific models (like a realistic car, a modern handgun, or interior furniture) that are offered for free as promotional samples.
*   **OpenGameArt (opengameart.org):** The granddaddy of free game assets. The website UI is very dated, but the library is vast. It is community-driven and spans 2D, 3D, music, and sound effects.

---

### 💡 A Quick Note on Licensing
Before you publish a commercial game, always double-check the license of your downloaded assets:
*   **CC0 (Public Domain):** Do whatever you want. Modify it, put it in a paid game, no attribution required. 
*   **CC-BY:** Free to use commercially, but you **must** credit the creator in your game's credits.
*   **Non-Commercial (NC):** You cannot use these in a game you plan to sell or monetize.
*   **Engine-Specific Licenses:** Be careful when downloading free content from the *Unreal Engine Marketplace / Fab* or *Unity Asset Store*. Some assets are strictly licensed to only be used within their respective game engines.
